title: Seabreeze activation and onboarding sync
summary: Kickoff/walkthrough for Seabreeze’s activation. Covered staging access, SSO/SAML, VPC networking, KMS integration, and pilot success criteria. Agreed on runbook updates and a short pilot (3 weeks) with latency & cost metrics capture. Action items assigned for runbook, infra access, and security questionnaire.

Seabreeze infra to open a staging VPC peering ticket and assign access by 2026-07-21
Schedule 1-hour staging handoff with infra (Jordan + Mei + Tanya) week of 2026-07-22
Security team (Oliver) to receive SOC2 and KMS integration docs from Redwood

Jordan Lee (CSM) | Set up staging handoff meeting and invite infra owners | Due: 2026-07-21

header:
Date: 2026-07-18 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45 min | Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alice Morales (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM); Raj Patel, Mei Chen, Oliver Grant, Tanya Ruiz (Seabreeze)
transcript:
[00:00] Alice Morales: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I see a full table, awesome. Quick check, are we on the right timezone?
[00:08] Raj Patel: Yep 3pm UTC works fine for us.
[00:12] Alice Morales: Cool. So agenda — staging access, SSO, KMS, pilot scope, and next steps. Jordan you good to lead the runbook bits?
[00:21] Jordan Lee: Yep, I’ll jump in. First question to Seabreeze — what environment do you want us to deploy to for the pilot, hosted or private?
[00:30] Mei Chen: We prefer a private VPC peering option initially. We need to keep traffic inside our cloud for compliance.
[00:36] Alice Morales: Makes sense, private deployment is supported — Redwood Private with VPC peering or on-prem agent if needed. Small note: our internals sometimes say "Reedwood Private" on auto notes, ignore typos there.
[00:46] Oliver Grant: From security side, we need KMS integration details and key rotation policies. Also SOC 2 artifacts.
[00:52] Jordan Lee: We’ll send SOC2 and the architecture whitepaper. For KMS we support AWS KMS and customer-managed keys; we also have HSM options for enterprise.
[01:03] Tanya Ruiz: For network, we'll need a step-by-step peering guide and the minimum ports.
[01:09] Alice Morales: Absolutely. Jordan will include a staging checklist with the required CIDR ranges and firewall rules. I want to flag that in some previous notes the KV cache got mis-typed as "KV cash" in the docs — we’ll make sure the runbook is clean.
[01:22] Raj Patel: Great. Pilot length — we were thinking 3 weeks to validate latency/cost and fidelity. Is that a workable scope?
[01:29] Jordan Lee: That's a good window. We recommend a 3-week pilot with 2 phases: Phase 1 smoke + integration, Phase 2 load/fidelity with 1k request/day ramp.
[01:38] Mei Chen: One ask — can we pin a model version and get determinism? We want to reproduce results for regressions.
[01:44] Alice Morales: Yes, you can pin model versions and we have rollout controls and canary policies. I’ll add instructions to the runbook for pinning and rollback.
[01:52] Oliver Grant: About logs — we need audit logs for all token-level activity and retention options.
[01:58] Jordan Lee: We produce request traces and per-route logs. Retention is configurable; for pilot we can set 30 days and discuss longer retention if you need. There might be an add-on for extended retention.
[02:10] Raj Patel: Cost — quick ballpark for pilot? We want to compare hosted vs dedicated.
[02:16] Alice Morales: For short pilots, hosted and Redwood Dedicated both work. Hosted gets you fast onboarding, dedicated gives predictable throughput. I’ll include a cost estimator in the runbook and a simple tokens-per-minute baseline from our experience.
[02:27] Mei Chen: Any early gotchas you’ve seen with VPC peering?
[02:31] Jordan Lee: Mostly firewall rules and IAM role scoping. Also, one customer forgot to open ephemeral port ranges for the runtime and saw dropped connections. We’ll include exact ports.
[02:40] Tanya Ruiz: Good to know. On SSO — we use Okta and SAML. What’s the Redwood flow?
[02:45] Alice Morales: We support SAML SSO (IdP initiated and SP). We’ll provide metadata XML and the attribute mappings. Sometimes the auto-transcript calls it "Redwood Console" as "Redwood Consolee" — ignore that, docs are fine.
[02:56] Oliver Grant: For KMS, do you require us to rotate keys or can Redwood manage?
[03:01] Jordan Lee: Both supported. For higher compliance, customers manage their own KMS keys and we integrate through cross-account roles.
[03:08] Raj Patel: Excellent. On instrumentation, we'd like latency percentiles and per-model breakdown in the console.
[03:13] Alice Morales: Yep, token-level latency, P50/P95/P99, model breakdowns. Jordan will point you to the Console dashboards and how to wire alerts.
[03:24] Mei Chen: Action items?
[03:27] Jordan Lee: I'll recap — we’ll send the runbook, peering steps, SAML metadata, and SOC2 pack. Seabreeze will provision staging VPC and assign a contact.
[03:38] Raj Patel: For the pilot datasets, do you recommend obfuscation before sending?
[03:42] Alice Morales: If there's any PII, yes. You can obfuscate locally or use pseudo-random replacements. We can also run locally on-prem if needed.
[03:51] Tanya Ruiz: Who will be our day-to-day contact at Redwood during the pilot?
[03:55] Alice Morales: Jordan (CSM) will be your primary for operations and I'll be the AE for escalation and commercial items.
[04:02] Jordan Lee: I’ll set up a shared Slack channel for quick comms.
[04:06] Mei Chen: One last technical — is continuous batching enabled by default? We have spiky workloads and don’t want latency surprises.
[04:12] Alice Morales: There's an auto-batching runtime; defaults are tuned for low latency. You can control batching windows per route. We'll include tuning recommendations based on your payload sizes.
[04:22] Oliver Grant: Please make sure any demo creds are time-limited.
[04:25] Jordan Lee: Of course.
[04:27] Alice Morales: OK, sounds like we have alignment. Recap of next steps in chat after this call and I’ll follow up with the runbook bundle.
[04:34] Raj Patel: Thanks all, appreciate it.
[04:36] Alice Morales: Thanks everyone — talk soon.
